default.reason: ops-desk: fak Ops worker desk - the desk defaults to the middle-ground tier (glm-5.3-flash) and rotates among the elected same-class seats by the shape of the work (deepseek-v4.1-flash for hard/long-context implementation and the destructive/high-risk floor). Both seats are hosted flash-class models the SAME provider carries (hive-ai hosts zai-org/glm-5.3-flash AND deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one OpenAI-compatible wire), so the desk rotates through them - see internal/modelroute/rotation.go (NextSeat/RotationPeers). Unmatched normal fak-Ops work -> glm-5.3-flash, the middle ground.

plan.reason: destructive/irreversible tool call (delete): the security-release floor never drops to the fast middle seat however small the call looks -> hard/long-context seat deepseek-v4.1-flash, the rotation pool's floor principle: with deepseek-v4-pro and gpt-6-astra unavailable, the floor escalates to the strongest available same-provider peer in the hosted-flash pool, never below it
destructive tool call (drop): same security-release floor as delete -> deepseek-v4.1-flash; never the fast middle seat for a drop-shaped call

caller tagged the aspect high-risk (push/release/migration or a security/policy surface): irreversible outward-facing work rides deepseek-v4.1-flash. The hard/long-context seat carries the highest-stakes band of the hosted-flash pool; it never lands on the fast middle seat by inheritance

hard/long-horizon fak-Ops work (large refactor, migration, cross-cutting design, deep debugging) -> deepseek-v4.1-flash: the 1M-context seat of the hosted-flash pool carries the hardest band. Placed before the read/search rules so a high-flagged aspect escalates even when it is read-shaped

fak-Ops facade work: the desk attests the routed seat for the workspace surface (root turn, plan audit, view-only candidates) -> deepseek-v4.1-flash carries the facade; state/routed facade rows are the operator-facing triage surface

moderate fak-Ops work (ordinary feature/bugfix/focused edit) -> deepseek-v4.1-flash, the long-context implementation seat. Named explicitly (a floor >= medium) so medium work lands on the impl seat instead of falling through to the low->glm-5.3-flash rule below

low-complexity fak-Ops aspect (small mechanical edit, quick lookup) -> glm-5.3-flash, the fast middle seat of the hosted-flash pool; reached only after the medium rule, so it bands to genuinely-low work
read-shaped tool call (read/inspect): cheap, low-stakes, not destructive and not flagged hard -> glm-5.3-flash (fast); a wrong read costs a re-run, not a bad write
search/lookup tool call: cheap read-shaped work -> glm-5.3-flash, the fast middle seat
short interactive fak-Ops turn (quick question/tiny edit, no complexity flag) -> glm-5.3-flash for low latency
